Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Communication and Practices--

Q203a: How often do you or clinic staff educate TB patients on cough etiquette, i.e., covering their mouth with hand, tissue, or elbow when coughing or sneezing, etc.?
Q203b: How often are windows in your clinic kept open or fans and exhausts turned on to blow air in the direction away from others when treating TB presumptive or confirmed cases?
Q203c: How often do clinic staff give priority to coughing patients, i.e., attend to patients who are coughing first?
Q203d: How often do clinic staff discuss with family members or those living with your TB patients, about basic information, and skills to protect household members and contacts from infection?
Q203e: How often do clinic staff screen all family members of confirmed TB patients for TB symptoms?
Q204: How many visits are typically required to confirm a suspected case of TB?

Patient’s Psycho-social assessment- when patients come with symptoms of TB ---

Q205a: How often do you take patient’s previous medical/psychosocial history [including whether they had TB before]

Q205d: How often do you assess patient’s ability to follow the TB treatment plan, including barriers to treatment (such as lack of transportation, expensive TB medications, etc.)?
Q205e: How often do you assess patients attitudes/beliefs towards TB including facing social stigma?
Q205f: How often do you assess patient’s family support such as financial, nutritional, treatment supporter, dealing with social stigma etc.?

Describe about the DBT scheme for the provider or informant benefits – for those who are not aware of the schemes / are aware incompletely. 
All private sector providers, registered on Nikshay will be eligible to receive the incentives, as under – 
• Rs. 500 for notification of TB patient and, 
• Rs. 500 for reporting treatment outcome of their own current patient. 
A private provider may authorize any staff of his establishment to receive the incentives

BEST-WORST SCALING EXERCISE ------The government would like to increase the rate at which providers register and follow up with TB patients on Nikshay. However, they have a limited budget they can dedicate to this effort. Below we are going to ask you 10 questions.
